lines.en: Good morning! Welcome to Union Station. Is that heavy suitcase giving you trouble?
lines.pt: Bom dia! Bem-vinda à Union Station. Essa mala pesada está atrapalhando?

lines.en: Could you tell me the time, please? My phone died, and that clock looks wrong.
lines.pt: Poderia me dizer as horas, por favor? Meu celular descarregou, e aquele relógio parece errado.

lines.en: It's ten forty-five. The big clock is five minutes slow. Are you catching the train to Chattanooga?
lines.pt: São dez e quarenta e cinco. O relógio grande está cinco minutos atrasado. Vai pegar o trem para Chattanooga?

lines.en: Yes! Could you tell me where the ticket office is? I need to pick one up.
lines.pt: Sim! Poderia me dizer onde fica a bilheteria de passagens? Preciso retirar uma.

lines.en: It's right behind you, next to the coffee shop. The machines are faster.
lines.pt: Fica logo atrás de você, ao lado da cafeteria. As máquinas são mais rápidas.

lines.en: Could you tell me if it's a fast train? I have a meeting at two.
lines.pt: Poderia me dizer se é um trem rápido? Tenho uma reunião às duas.

lines.en: It's the express. It makes only three stops and takes about two hours.
lines.pt: É o expresso. Faz só três paradas e leva umas duas horas.

lines.en: Wonderful. Which platform does it leave from? There are so many numbers on the board.
lines.pt: Maravilhoso. De qual plataforma ele sai? Há tantos números no painel.

lines.en: Platform six, down the stairs on your right. It leaves in twenty minutes.
lines.pt: Plataforma seis, descendo a escada à direita. Ele sai em vinte minutos.

lines.en: Thank you! Is it a long walk? I don't want to run with this suitcase.
lines.pt: Obrigada! É uma caminhada longa? Não quero correr com esta mala.

lines.en: Only about two minutes. Have a safe trip! When you hear the whistle, they're boarding.
lines.pt: Só uns dois minutos. Boa viagem! Quando ouvir o apito, estão embarcando.

teach.goal: Ponte português → inglês com palavras úteis.
solo: Peça uma frase pessoal com 2 das palavras.

facts.big: Could you tell me + where/when/if + sujeito + verbo?
facts.label: Could you tell me…?
facts.sub: Para pedir informação com educação, use Could you tell me + palavra de pergunta + sujeito + verbo: Could you tell me where the ticket office is? Could you tell me if it’s fast?

facts.label: Educado
facts.sub: Para pedir informação com educação, use Could you tell me + informação: Could you tell me the time? Could é mais gentil que can. Acrescente please para soar ainda melhor.

facts.label: Ordem
facts.sub: Depois de Could you tell me, use a ordem de frase afirmativa: where the office is, what time it is, how much a ticket costs. Não use a ordem de pergunta direta.

compare.br: No Brasil, pedimos “Pode me dizer onde fica a bilheteria?”.
compare.tip: Diga: “Could you tell me where the ticket office is?”
compare.us: Em inglês: Could you tell me + palavra (where/when/if) + sujeito + verbo.

solo: Peça uma experiência pessoal do aluno com essa diferença.
group: Leia as duas colunas e peça que apontem a maior diferença.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: Could you tell me… is a polite request.
We say “Could you tell me where is the office?”
items.why: We say where the office is.

items.s: After Could you tell me, we can use if.
items.why: Yes: Could you tell me if…?

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: Could you tell me… is a polite request. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
We say “Could you tell me where is the office?” → Falso (We say where the office is.)
After Could you tell me, we can use if. → Verdadeiro (Yes: Could you tell me if…?)

pages.title: A train station · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a rainy afternoon at the train station in Nashville. People walk fast with umbrellas and bags. Vic stands near the clock with a coffee. Lia arrives with a big blue suitcase. She is tired and a little nervous. She walks up to Vic to ask something.
“Excuse me. Could you tell me the time, please?” says Vic. “Sure. It’s ten past two.” says Lia. “Thanks. Could you tell me when the next train to Memphis leaves?” says Vic.

pages.title: A train station · 3/3
paragraphs: “Look at the board. Could you tell me what time you must arrive?” says Lia. “By four o’clock. Could you tell me one more thing? Is there Wi-Fi here?” says Vic. Vic points to the ticket office. Lia buys a ticket and a sandwich. Her train is on platform four. She waves goodbye to Vic. The rain finally stops. Polite questions make travel easier.
